Other instance\\n types can be attached to volumes provisioned with up to 64,000 IOPS, but can achieve up to 32,000\\n IOPS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I choose the right Amazon EBS volume type for my workload?\",\"context\":\"### Compare provisioned IOPS SSD volumes\\n\\n[Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html) include **io2** Block Express volumes and **io1** volumes. If you require more durability and a higher IOPS-to-GiB ratio, then use **io2** Block Express.\\n\\n**Note:** All **io2** volumes created after November 21, 2023, are **io2** Block Express volumes. To troubleshoot latency issues on an EBS volume, calculate the maximum available IOPS and throughput quota.\\n\\nThe available IOPS and throughput for an EBS volume can vary depending on volume type, volume size, and provisioned IOPS.\\n\\nTo find the maximum available IOPS and throughput for your EBS volume, use the following interactive bash script. Then, analyze the performance of your EBS volume based on the quotas. For more information, see [VolumeLimitCalculator](https://github.com/awslabs/aws-support-tools/tree/master/EBS/VolumeLimitCalculator) on the GitHub website.\\n\\nComplete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Download the **VolumeLimitCalculator** script to your Linux instance, and convert it to a format that you can run:\\n ```plaintext\\n # chmod +x volume_Limit_calculator.sh\\n ```\\n \\n2. Run the script:\\n ```plaintext\\n # ./volume_Limit_calculator.sh\\n ```\\n **Note:** The preceding script doesn't calculate IOPS and throughput for io2 block express volumes.\\n\\nRelated information\\n-------------------\\n\\n[Amazon EBS volume types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volume-types.html)\\n\\n[How do I optimize the performance of my Amazon EBS volumes?](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-performance)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-maximum-iops-throughput\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up EBS io2 IOPS quota documentation"}

{"id": "f9c84b58-ac7b-4eff-98d0-dca074c75c40", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is a regional, account-level quota, and you can raise it. In us-east-1 in account 012345678901_1, "IOPS for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes" is set to 100,000 (quota code L-8D977E7E). It's marked adjustable. I only checked that region, so if you hit the error elsewhere, check that region too.

**What to do**

1. **Request a quota increase.** Ask for at least 150,000 IOPS, plus headroom if you plan to create more io2 volumes. You can do this in the Service Quotas console under Amazon EBS, or with the CLI:
   ```
   aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase \
     --service-code ebs --quota-code L-8D977E7E \
     --desired-value 200000 --region <your-region>
   ```
   Small increases are often approved automatically. Larger ones may go to AWS Support for review.

2. **Check the other io2 quotas.** Your storage quota is 20 TiB per region (L-09BD8365). A 150K IOPS volume may need more capacity than you expect. io2 allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB, so 150K IOPS needs at least 150 GiB. If your volume is large, or you already have other io2 volumes, you might hit the storage quota next.

3. **Check that your instance can use that many IOPS.** Volumes with more than 64,000 IOPS only work fully on Nitro-based instances. They can be provisioned up to 256,000 IOPS per volume. Other instance types can attach to the volume but top out at about 32,000 IOPS. Also check that the instance's own EBS bandwidth and IOPS limits are high enough for 150K.

**If you need a workaround before the increase is approved**

- Use fewer IOPS for now, up to the remaining headroom under your current quota.
- Free up IOPS by lowering the provisioned IOPS on, or retiring, other io2 volumes in the region.

Existing io2 volumes count against the same regional quota, so the quota applies to the combined IOPS of all your io2 volumes. Your 150K request fails because it plus your current usage goes over 100,000.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
